+== Amendment (2026-06-04): support matrix locked in
+
+The JetBrains side now formally targets **all JetBrains IDEs (TextMate floor)
++ IDEA Ultimate (LSP ceiling)**. The default Gradle build (`buildPlugin`)
+produces a TextMate-only plugin compatible with every Community + Ultimate
+IDE; the `-PwithLsp` build adds the `flatbars-lsp` server consumed via the
+Ultimate-only platform LSP API. `runPluginVerifier` is wired against the
+since-build range so any compatibility regression fails before publish.
+
+Community-edition users see an `EditorNotificationProvider` banner on first
+opening a FlatBars file, linking to the Ultimate upgrade path so the missing
+LSP capabilities never surface as a silent gap.
+
+
+== Amendment (2026-06-04): editor floor refined to ERB-canonical scopes
+
+The TextMate floor switched from FlatBars-bespoke `meta.function.*` /
+`meta.variable.unescaped.*` scopes to the canonical ERB/PHP/EJS pattern:
+every brace cluster carries `punctuation.section.embedded.{begin,end}`,
+every tag region carries `meta.embedded.{line,block}`, and control-tag
+sigils split out as `keyword.control.{section,inheritance,import}`. Themes
+that style ERB braces now style FlatBars braces identically with zero
+hardcoded colour in either editor manifest.
+
+`#tag_interior` patterns added on every expression-bearing tag rule paint
+the body's literals (`string.quoted.*`, `constant.numeric.*`,
+`constant.language.*` for `true`/`false`/`null`), operators
+(`keyword.operator.*`), subexpression parens (`punctuation.section.parens`),
+list-literal brackets (`punctuation.section.brackets`), and path separators
+(`punctuation.accessor`).
+
+LSP `shrinkToInner` trims `{`/`}`/`~`/whitespace off every tag-level
+semantic-token span before emission, so the `keyword`/`set-delimiter`/`error`
+spans cover only the inner body and leave the braces to the grammar's
+embedded scope. `paintOperations` adds a new `operation` semantic kind that
+paints helper names from `operations.json` in head / subexpression-head /
+pipe-target positions; gated by the catalogue so plain variables stay
+default-coloured.
+
+
+== Amendment (2026-06-04): short-form dialect extensions + hybrid templates
+
+Each dialect now ships two equivalent native extensions — the long form
+(`.rawbars`/`.minbars`/`.fullbars`/`.maxbars`) and a short alias
+(`.rbars`/`.mbars`/`.fbars`/`.xbars`). Both resolve to the same language id;
+both are listed in every consumer (`shared/sync.mjs`, VS Code's
+`package.json`, JetBrains's TextMate bundle, the grammar's `fileTypes`,
+LSP's `dialectForUri`). The packagers' language tables are now codegenerated
+from the single `LANGUAGES` source so adding an extension touches one place.
+
+`editors/flatbars-injection.tmLanguage.json` is an injection grammar with
+`injectTo` covering 26 common host scopes (`source.java`, `source.ruby`,
+`source.python`, …, `text.html.basic`). Paired with `files.associations`
+(`*.java.xbars` → `java`), the host paints its native syntax and the
+injection layers `{{…}}` tag highlighting on top. The LSP attaches to the
+host — hybrid templates are syntax-only for tag intelligence; users wanting
+full IntelliSense open with the dialect's language id.
+
+
+== Amendment (2026-06-04): capability matrix split into ADR-026
+
+The full list of LSP capabilities we ship vs deliberately omit (the latter
+being principled design decisions tied to the engine's deliberately
+absent cross-template scope graph) lives in
+xref:adr-0026-editor-capability-matrix.adoc[ADR-026].

+= ADR-026 — Editor capability matrix
+:adr-id: 0026
+:status: Accepted
+:date: 2026-06-04
+
+== Context
+
+ADR-017 set the two-layer model — TextMate grammar (the floor) plus
+`flatbars-lsp` semantic tokens (the ceiling) — and shipped the minimum LSP
+surface needed to demonstrate it: `semanticTokens/full`, `publishDiagnostics`,
+`textDocument/hover`, `textDocument/completion`, and a `codeAction`
+canonicalisation quick-fix.
+
+The June 2026 editor-plugin review surfaced a follow-up question: what is the
+*complete* set of LSP capabilities the editors advertise, and which IDE-native
+features (Find Usages, Rename, Reformat, Structure View, Folding, Breadcrumbs,
+Go to Definition) is the plugin expected to provide? The platform LSP client in
+JetBrains does not auto-wire most of those; the server must both advertise the
+capability and the editor side must opt in.
+
+This ADR fixes the matrix.
+
+== Decision
+
+The editors ship the following LSP capabilities, gated on what the engine can
+honestly compute from a *single* template document (the FlatBars engine does
+not maintain a cross-template scope graph, by design — partials are looked up
+by name in a host-supplied registry, see ADR-003):
+
+|===
+| Capability | Status | Source
+
+| `semanticTokens/full`
+| Ship
+| ADR-017 — engine `tokenize` + vocab-driven legend.
+
+| `publishDiagnostics`
+| Ship
+| ADR-023 — recovering parser → `NodeError` ranges.
+
+| `textDocument/hover`
+| Ship
+| `operations.json` derived from `FullBars.preludeSchema`.
+
+| `textDocument/completion`
+| Ship
+| Same source as hover, gated on `inTagContext`.
+
+| `textDocument/codeAction`
+| Ship
+| Canonicalisation rewrites (`index` → `index0`, `partial-block` → `yield`).
+
+| `textDocument/foldingRange`
+| Ship (new)
+| Every block-open / block-close pair is a fold region; raw-block regions fold.
+  Single-document, structurally trivial from the engine tokens.
+
+| `textDocument/documentSymbol`
+| Ship (new)
+| The block nesting hierarchy projected as a symbol tree — feeds IntelliJ
+  Structure View and VS Code outline.
+
+| `textDocument/formatting`
+| Ship (new)
+| Canonical-spacing inside `{{ … }}` (one space after the opener, one before
+  the closer, normalised internal whitespace). Single-document, deterministic.
+
+| `textDocument/definition`
+| Do not ship
+| Would require a cross-template scope graph (which partial defines which
+  identifier, where a `{{> partial}}` resolves). FlatBars uses a runtime
+  partial registry the engine never indexes; building an editor-time index
+  duplicates the host's data and would drift. Out of scope for the editor.
+
+| `textDocument/references`
+| Do not ship
+| Same reason as definition: no global identifier graph.
+
+| `textDocument/rename`
+| Do not ship
+| Same reason; refactoring partial names would have to coordinate with the
+  host application's partial registry.
+
+| `textDocument/documentHighlight`
+| Do not ship
+| Without a scope graph, single-buffer "highlight uses of `name`" devolves to
+  string search — strictly worse than the editor's built-in word highlight.
+|===
+
+The "do not ship" decisions are *principled*, not deferred: the engine model
+deliberately keeps partials and helpers as host-registry lookups, so the
+editor has no honest source of truth for those refactorings. Documenting that
+here turns the absence into a feature.
+
+== Consequences
+
+* **VS Code**: All "ship" capabilities surface through `vscode-languageclient`
+  with no additional wiring — VS Code consumes advertised server capabilities
+  automatically.
+* **JetBrains**: The platform LSP client auto-consumes hover/completion/
+  diagnostics/codeAction. The new capabilities (`foldingRange`,
+  `documentSymbol`, `formatting`) require an `LspCustomization` opt-in or the
+  corresponding `Lsp4j*` extension in the descriptor; ADR-017's editor-side
+  amendment tracks the JetBrains-specific wiring as a maintenance item.
+* **Verifier**: `check:operations-paint` (added alongside this ADR) keeps the
+  catalog / painter parity honest, so the helper-name highlighting stays
+  trustworthy even as the prelude grows.
+* **Future**: Adding a cross-template scope graph (a real "module system" for
+  FlatBars) would unlock `definition`, `references`, `rename`. That is a
+  language-level change behind a fresh ADR, not an editor follow-up.
+
+== Status
+
+Accepted 2026-06-04. Effective immediately.
